newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan sets short-term rate target at 5.0-5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sets short-term rate target at 5.0-5.5 pct.

text.p: Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Tuesday the bank would control short-term interest rates at between 5.00 and 5.50 percent level before the February 7 Chinese New Year.
The overnight interbank rate, the indicator for the domestic short-term rates, had surged to over 10 percent in previous years.
In 1995, the overnight rate reached as high as 8.0 percent.
Sheu said he did not expected the money rates to reach previous high levels in part because of a sluggish domestic economy.

He added some T$100 billion negotiable certificates of deposits would mature during the peak period and the central bank plans to inject T$22 billion in postal funds into the banking system to ease expected tight liquidity.
The bank, which has said it wants to maintain a stable-to-loose monetary policy, has been acting persistently to keep the rates stable.
On Monday, the overnight interbank rate closed at 5.219 percent against Saturday's 5.163 close, with 30-day commercial paper unchanged at 5.00-5.10.
